date_note: Date is the day of the Korea Federation of Savings Banks' notice as Toyo Economy reports it (19 November); the Federation says the time of the incident is not yet confirmed.
title: Savings bank staff details leak after hack of KG Edu One training management site
summary: The Korea Federation of Savings Banks said on 19 November that a savings bank education management site run by KG Edu One was hit by an external hacking attack, Toyo Economy reports; Dailysecu also reported the hack. Leaked data include employees' bank names, positions and names. The Federation says the number affected and how the breach happened are not yet confirmed, and the site is separate from the banks' transaction networks.
plain: A training-management site run for South Korea's savings banks was hacked, leaking staff names, positions and bank names. The banks' federation says the site is separate from the banks' transaction systems.
exec: A supplier's training site exposed bank employee identities, which can fuel impersonation scams against customers and staff.
action: The Korea Federation of Savings Banks says banks never ask by phone or text for account passwords, security card numbers, OTPs or authentication codes; verify suspected impersonation via the bank's official main phone number.

validation.note: Follow-up 22 Nov: Toyo Economy (19 Nov) relays the Korea Federation of Savings Banks' notice; Dailysecu (read 20 Nov) reports the same hack from savings banks' notices. The Federation's own notice was not read. Number of banks and staff and the incident date are not stated.
